observations: Small portable electronic keyboard with full-size white/black keys, sitting on a red plastic chair.
YAMAHA logo clearly visible on the body in photos 0, 1, and 2.
Printed voice/style selection charts in purple and teal cover much of the top panel, typical of an entry-level/beginner keyboard.
Small LCD display and basic button cluster, no large control panel or many sliders/knobs typical of 'professional' arranger keyboards.
No model number or series name (e.g., PSR-xxx) visible or readable in any photo.
No power adapter, stand, or box shown in any photo.
Keys show some yellowing/wear consistent with an older, used unit.

claims.evidence: Photos 0-2 show a small, entry-level style keyboard with printed song/rhythm charts and a basic LCD, not the layout of a professional arranger or stage keyboard; no model number supports a 'professional' tier.
YAMAHA logo visible in photos 0, 1, and 2.

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or may have non-functional keys/buttons
risks.proof: A short video of the keyboard powering on and keys/buttons being pressed with sound

risks.risk: Missing power adapter or stand needed for use
risks.proof: Photo showing the adapter and/or stand included with sale

risks.risk: Exact model/series unknown, affecting feature set and value
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model number sticker, usually on the back or bottom of the keyboard

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage (cracks, broken keys) not visible from current angles
risks.proof: Photos from additional angles including the back, underside, and close-ups of all keys
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming cosmetic wear only, no structural damage confirmed

proof_requests: Clear photo of the model number label (usually back or underside of keyboard)
Video of the keyboard powering on and producing sound across several keys
Photo confirming presence of power adapter and/or stand
Additional photos of the back and underside for hidden damage
response.reason: Brand is visually confirmed as Yamaha and the item can be priced as a generic used entry-level portable keyboard at worst case (untested, no accessories shown), but the 'professional' claim is contradicted by the visible design and lack of any model identification.
